answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it may claim rewards. A bridge operator verifies that the bond came from completed, independently checked tasks, then lets peers slash it when an identity double-claims or coordinates fraud. Creating a thousand Sybils therefore means funding a thousand bonds and risking their loss, not merely generating names. A haven or knoll of cheap accounts offers no advantage if each must earn and expose real stake.
